\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{аренда} (arénda)}{аренда (arénda)}]{\ru{аренда} (arénda) — rent, a lease}

\label{lesson:RU-C398-arenda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for paid, then the Russian for profitable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{аренда}}
\textbf{\ru{аренда}} (\emph{arénda}) — \textquotedblleft{}rent, a lease\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Аренда} \ru{квартиры} \ru{в} \ru{центре} \ru{очень} \ru{дорогая}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Arénda kvartíry v tséntre óchen dorogáya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Renting a flat in the centre is very expensive.
\end{quote}

Feminine. \emph{\ru{Сдавать} \ru{в} \ru{аренду}} — to let; \emph{\ru{брать} \ru{в} \ru{аренду}} — to rent.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{аренда}} was borrowed from Polish \emph{arenda}, from Medieval Latin \emph{arrenda} (EtymDB), which is usually traced to Latin \emph{reddere} \textquotedblleft{}to give back, to pay\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arénda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arénda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{arénda}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for paid, then the Russian for profitable, then say \emph{arénda} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{арендовать} (arendovát)}{арендовать (arendovát)}]{\ru{арендовать} (arendovát) — to rent, to lease}

\label{lesson:RU-C398-arendovat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for profitable, then the Russian for rent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{арендовать}}
\textbf{\ru{арендовать}} (\emph{arendovát}) — \textquotedblleft{}to rent, to lease\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Мы} \ru{арендуем} \ru{маленький} \ru{офис}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My arendúyem málenkiy ófis.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We rent a small office.
\end{quote}

Imperfective and perfective; present \emph{\ru{арендую}, \ru{арендуешь}}. For a flat, people usually say \emph{\ru{снимать}}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{арендовать}} is built on \emph{\ru{аренда}} \textquotedblleft{}a lease\textquotedblright{} with the verb suffix \emph{-\ru{овать}}; the noun came through Polish \emph{arenda} from Medieval Latin (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{ипотека} (ipotéka)}{ипотека (ipotéka)}]{\ru{ипотека} (ipotéka) — a mortgage}

\label{lesson:RU-C398-ipoteka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for rent, then the Russian for to rent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{ипотека}}
\textbf{\ru{ипотека}} (\emph{ipotéka}) — \textquotedblleft{}a mortgage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Они} \ru{купили} \ru{квартиру} \ru{в} \ru{ипотеку}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Oní kupíli kvartíru v ipotéku.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They bought a flat with a mortgage.
\end{quote}

Feminine. \emph{\ru{Взять} \ru{ипотеку}} — to take out a mortgage.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{ипотека}} is usually traced to Greek \emph{hypoth\'{\={e}}kē} \textquotedblleft{}a pledge, a deposit\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{hypotithénai} \textquotedblleft{}to put under, to pledge\textquotedblright{}: the flat is put down as a pledge.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{страховать} (strakhovát)}{страховать (strakhovát)}]{\ru{страховать} (strakhovát) — to insure}

\label{lesson:RU-C398-strakhovat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for to rent, then the Russian for a mortgage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{страховать}}
\textbf{\ru{страховать}} (\emph{strakhovát}) — \textquotedblleft{}to insure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{Мы} \ru{страхуем} \ru{дом} \ru{от} \ru{пожара}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My strakhúyem dom ot pozhára.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We insure the house against fire.
\end{quote}

Imperfective; present \emph{\ru{страхую}, \ru{страхуешь}}; perfective \emph{\ru{застраховать}}. \emph{\ru{Страховать} \ru{от}} + genitive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{страховать}} is built on \emph{\ru{страх}} \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Proto-Slavic: to insure is to guard against what you fear.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{страховка} (strakhóvka)}{страховка (strakhóvka)}]{\ru{страховка} (strakhóvka) — insurance; a safety rope}

\label{lesson:RU-C398-strakhovka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a mortgage, then the Russian for to insure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{страховка}}
\textbf{\ru{страховка}} (\emph{strakhóvka}) — \textquotedblleft{}insurance; a safety rope\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ru{У} \ru{меня} \ru{есть} \ru{медицинская} \ru{страховка}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U menyá yest meditsínskaya strakhóvka.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have medical insurance.
\end{quote}

Feminine. Colloquial for \emph{\ru{страхование}}. It is also a climber’s safety rope.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{страховка}} is built on \emph{\ru{страховать}} \textquotedblleft{}to insure\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{\ru{страх}} \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
